title: The brief-delivery knowledge page carries the ack receipt, not the transition receipt
action: This page is the canonical narrative of how a foreign agent gets its brief, and its delivery-receipt section is now wrong end to end. Rewrite that section under herding-prompt-stall D1-D4; CONTEXT.md quotes herdr's published contract verbatim and locks all four, so cite it rather than re-deriving. The stale text runs from the line `This is the "state-receipt delivery", and it replaced an earlier pane-text check.` through the paragraph ending `it never becomes a silent decision to wait anyway.` — roughly lines 60-90. What it claims today and what is now true: (a) it says the receipt is the agent's own reported state moving into `working` as a TRANSITION off a per-send baseline. That is retired. The transition is satisfied by the agent's own BOOT flap when the baseline is sampled before the boot's working window — proven live on 2026-08-21, job trust-par-2, where bee stamped pane_id into job.json while the pane still sat at an empty prompt. The receipt is now an ACK FILE THE WORKER WRITES (D4): the brief's first instruction is to write `ack-<round>.json` atomically before any other step, carrying who took the job, and delivery is that file appearing — or the round's result file appearing for an ultra-fast round. herdr lifecycle state is no longer the success signal at all. (b) it says `The ready gate is idle-only for the same reason.` That is retired by D2: herdr defines `idle` as ready-for-input AND the tab has been seen in the focused UI, `done` as the same underlying ready state for an unseen tab, and CLI reads never mark a tab seen — so a `--no-focus` bee worker pane normally reports `done`, and the gate accepts `idle` or `done`. (c) the bounded re-send paragraph must now say what ends the wait EARLY: herdr's `agent_prompt_stalled` when a submission from a non-working state produces no observed lifecycle change within five seconds (D1), and herdr's `blocked` state — a recognized approval or question UI — at every wait point (D3). Both are failure detectors, never success signals. Keep and sharpen the page's general lesson, which is still right and now stronger: any confirmation an actor can produce BY ITSELF — an echoed keystroke, its own boot transition — is not evidence the other side received anything; only an artifact the receiver wrote is. Name each retired claim's superseding decision inline so a later reader does not resurrect it. Do not restructure the page, renumber anything, or touch sections outside the delivery-receipt narrative.
verify: rg -n 'idle-only|idle only|transition into working|TRANSITION off a per-send baseline' docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/handing-a-foreign-agent-its-brief.md; rg -n 'ack-|agent_prompt_stalled|blocked' docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/handing-a-foreign-agent-its-brief.md
